# **Model Routing in Google Cloud using API Gateway**

&nbsp;

![][image1]

&nbsp;

Most production AI systems don't run on just one model anymore. You might plan with a frontier reasoning model, summarize with a fast, low-cost model, and keep a second provider as a fallback. But each provider has its own API. In practice, that choice ends up as SDK sprawl in your code, or as a self-hosted proxy that you have to run, scale, and secure.

In this post, I walk through **model routing in API Gateway** (**Public Preview**). It's a managed way to route your API calls to the target model by simply changing the endpoint and without worrying much about the API implementation. You can create a single OpenAI compatible API call and simply switch the API path to access the underlying models such as Gemini, Anthropic, OpenAI and other AI models in Model Garden.&nbsp;

# **What is model routing, and why do you need it?**

## **The problem: many models, many APIs**

On Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI), each model family has its own endpoint and request format:

* **Google Gemini:** Gemini request format

* **Anthropic Claude:** Anthropic Messages request format

* **OpenAI-compatible MaaS models, such as gpt-oss:** OpenAI Chat Completions request format

&nbsp;

If your application uses all three, it needs three code paths. Teams usually end up with one of two patterns:

* **SDK sprawl:** every app embeds several SDKs. Every model swap means a code change and a redeploy.  
* **A self-hosted proxy such as LiteLLM:** clients get one API, but you now host, scale, patch, and secure one more service.

[Model routing for API Gateway](https://docs.cloud.google.com/api-gateway/docs/model-routing-overview) is a managed traffic management layer. It accepts OpenAI-compatible prompt requests, translates them in flight, and routes them to specific models in Model Garden. While there are other third party routers available out there, if your infrastructure is Google Cloud based, native Model Routing in Google Cloud provides you out of the box hassle free experience.

![Model routing architecture: clients send OpenAI-compatible requests to API Gateway. Its model router reads the model field, matches a rule, translates the request, and calls Gemini, Claude, or gpt-oss in Model Garden with the gateway service account.][image2]

*Fig 1: Architecture diagram showing client requests routed through API Gateway to various LLM providers in Model Garden.*

# **Why model routing in Google Cloud?**

A model router is only as useful as the models it can reach, and this is where Google Cloud stands out. Google Cloud is now the only hyperscale cloud provider, offering access to all three leading closed source LLMs, alongside more than 200 first-party, third-party, and open models on a unified enterprise AI platform.

![Model Garden brings together models from Google, Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI, Meta, DeepSeek, Mistral AI, and Z.ai under the same enterprise controls. Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI are supported as model routing targets.][image3]

*Fig 2: Overview of diverse model families supported on the enterprise AI platform.*

# **What is API Gateway?**

[API Gateway](https://docs.cloud.google.com/api-gateway/docs/about-api-gateway) is a fully managed Google Cloud service that puts a consistent, secure REST API in front of your backend services. You describe the API in an OpenAPI spec, and API Gateway hosts it. It also handles authentication (API keys, Google ID tokens, and other JWTs), quotas, traffic management, logging, and monitoring.

API Gateway added several AI-focused features in 2026, all in **Public Preview**:

* **Model routing** (Released: Aug 3, 2026): Routes OpenAI-compatible requests to models in Model Garden

* **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** (Released: Sep 11, 2026): Exposes existing REST APIs to agents as MCP tools

* **Streaming gateways** (Released: Sep 29, 2026): Streams traffic (SSE, chunked transfer, WebSockets, gRPC) instead of buffering it

&nbsp;

# **Configure model routing**

In this blog I will show you how to configure model routing in API Gateway.&nbsp;

![Configuration workflow: prepare once (enable models, enable APIs, create a service account, write apispec.yaml), deploy with the console, gcloud, or the Antigravity CLI, then verify.][image4]

*Fig 3: Configuration and deployment workflow for Model Routing.*

## **Prepare**

### **Step 1: Enable the models in Model Garden**

You can call Gemini models as soon as the Agent Platform API is enabled. Partner models such as Claude and managed open models such as gpt-oss must first be enabled in Model Garden.

![][image5]

*Fig 4: Enabling partner models like Grok 4.6 in Model Garden.*

### **Step 2: Enable the required APIs**

* **API Gateway API** (apigateway.googleapis.com): Creates and runs gateways

* **Service Management API** (servicemanagement.googleapis.com): Stores the managed service config for your API

* **Service Control API** (servicecontrol.googleapis.com): Checks requests (auth, quotas, telemetry) at run time

* **Agent Platform API** (aiplatform.googleapis.com): Serves the Model Garden endpoints

&nbsp;

In the console, go to **APIs & Services \> Library**, search for each API, and click **Enable**. Or use one command:

gcloud services enable \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;apigateway.googleapis.com \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;servicemanagement.googleapis.com \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;servicecontrol.googleapis.com \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;aiplatform.googleapis.com

### **Step 3: Create a service account for the gateway**

The gateway needs permission to make API calls to the models in Model Garden (Agent Platform). This is done by assigning a service account to the API Gateway. The API Gateway then will have all the permissions assigned to that Service Account. You can create and assign service account as follows.

&nbsp;

**With gcloud in the console.**

\# Create a dedicated identity for the gateway  
gcloud iam service-accounts create "\${SA\_NAME}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--display-name="API Gateway model router"

\# Let the gateway call models on Agent Platform, and nothing else  
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding "\${PROJECT\_ID}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--member="serviceAccount:\${SA\_EMAIL}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--role="roles/aiplatform.user"

\# Let your user attach this service account to an API config  
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding "\${SA\_EMAIL}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--member="user:\$(gcloud config get-value account)" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--role="roles/iam.serviceAccountUser"

In the Cloud Console:

1. Go to **IAM & Admin \> Service accounts** and click **Create service account**.  
2. Name it model-router-sa and grant it the **Agent Platform User** role.  
3. Open the new service account's **Permissions** tab and click **Grant access**.  
4. Grant your user the **Service Account User** role.

### **Step 4: Write the OpenAPI 3.x spec**

For the API paths, you can create an OpenAPI API spec YAML file with the necessary paths defined. You can add paths for all the models you need to support. For example you can take a look at a sample YAML file below. This YAML supports Gemini, Anthropic, OpenAI,&nbsp;&nbsp;

openapi: 3.0.3

&nbsp;

info:

&nbsp;&nbsp;title: OpenAPI 3.x spec using Model Routing

&nbsp;&nbsp;description: Using Model Routing in an OAS 3.x spec

&nbsp;&nbsp;version: 1.0.0

&nbsp;

x-google-api-management:

&nbsp;&nbsp;backends:

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;gemini-38-flash:

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;address: "https\://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/haren-main/locations/global/publishers/google/models/gemini-3.8-flash:generateContent"

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;deadline: 60.0

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;pathTranslation: CONSTANT\_ADDRESS

&nbsp;

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;anthropic-claude-opus-47:

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;address: "https\://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/haren-main/locations/global/publishers/anthropic/models/claude-opus-4-7:rawPredict"

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;deadline: 60.0

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;pathTranslation: CONSTANT\_ADDRESS

&nbsp;

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;anthropic-claude-sonnet-5:

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;address: "https\://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/haren-main/locations/global/publishers/anthropic/models/claude-sonnet-5:rawPredict"

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;deadline: 60.0

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;pathTranslation: CONSTANT\_ADDRESS

&nbsp;

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;anthropic-claude-haiku-45:

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;address: "https\://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/haren-main/locations/global/publishers/anthropic/models/claude-haiku-4-5:rawPredict"

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;deadline: 60.0

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;pathTranslation: CONSTANT\_ADDRESS

&nbsp;

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;vertex-maas-openapi:

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;address: "https\://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/haren-main/locations/global/endpoints/openapi/chat/completions"

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;deadline: 60.0

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;pathTranslation: CONSTANT\_ADDRESS

&nbsp;

&nbsp;&nbsp;ai:

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;models:

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;routing:

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;routers:

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;gemini-claude-router:

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;defaultModel:

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;backend: gemini-38-flash

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;targetModel: google/gemini-3.8-flash

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;rules:

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;\- model: "claude-opus-4-7"

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;backend: anthropic-claude-opus-47

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;targetModel: anthropic/claude-opus-4-7

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;\- model: "claude-sonnet-5"

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;backend: anthropic-claude-sonnet-5

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;targetModel: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;\- model: "claude-haiku-4-5"

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;backend: anthropic-claude-haiku-45

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;targetModel: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5

&nbsp;

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;maas-models-router:

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;defaultModel:

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;backend: vertex-maas-openapi

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;targetModel: openai/gpt-oss-120b-maas

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;rules:

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;\- model: "gpt-oss-120b-maas"

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;backend: vertex-maas-openapi

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;targetModel: openai/gpt-oss-120b-maas

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;\- model: "deepseek-v4.1"

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;backend: vertex-maas-openapi

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;targetModel: openai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-maas

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;\- model: "grok-4.7"

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;backend: vertex-maas-openapi

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;targetModel: openai/grok-4.7

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;\- model: "glm-5.2"

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;backend: vertex-maas-openapi

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;targetModel: openai/glm-5.2-maas

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;\- model: "llama-4-maverick"

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;backend: vertex-maas-openapi

&nbsp;

servers:

&nbsp;&nbsp;\- url: "https\://serving-host-name"

&nbsp;

paths:

&nbsp;&nbsp;/v1/chat/gemini-claude:

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;x-google-model-router: gemini-claude-router

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;responses:

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;responses:

## **Deploy**  **With Google Cloud console (web UI)**

1. Go to [API Gateway](https://console.cloud.google.com/api-gateway/) in the Google Cloud console and click **Create Gateway**.

![The API Gateway APIs page with the Create Gateway button.][image6]

*Fig 5: Google Cloud Console API Gateway main landing page.*

2. In the **API** section, select **Create new API**. Enter a display name (eg. ModelRouting) and an API ID (eg. modelrouting). The console previews the managed service name for the API.

![The API section with Create new API selected, display name ModelRouting, and API ID modelrouting.][image7]

*Fig 6: Defining API display name and API ID in the Cloud Console.*

3. In the **API Config** section, select **Create new API config** and click **Browse** to upload apispec.yaml (the YAML created in the previous step). Enter a display name. Under **Select a Service Account**, choose the service account you created or use an existing one with required permissions.

![][image8]

*Fig 7: Uploading the OpenAPI spec and assigning a gateway service account.*

4. In **Gateway details**, enter a display name, choose the location(eg. us-central1 ), and click **Create gateway**.

![The Gateway details section with location us-central1 and the Create gateway button.][image9]

*Fig 8: Setting gateway region location details in the Cloud Console.*

5. Creating the gateway takes a few minutes. When it finishes, the API appears in the list with its managed service name.

![The APIs list showing the modelrouting API and its managed service.][image10]

*Fig 9: View of newly created active API and managed service endpoint.*

6. Click the API name, open the **Gateways** tab, and copy the gateway URL.

## **With gcloud CLI**

Create the API, the API config, and the gateway:

\# 1\. Create the API (a logical container plus its managed service)  
gcloud api-gateway apis create "\${API\_ID}" \--display-name="ModelRouting"

\# 2\. Create an API config from the spec. API Gateway validates it here.  
gcloud api-gateway api-configs create "\${CONFIG\_ID}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--api="\${API\_ID}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--openapi-spec=apispec.yaml \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--backend-auth-service-account="\${SA\_EMAIL}"

\# 3\. Deploy the config to a regional gateway  
gcloud api-gateway gateways create "\${GATEWAY\_ID}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--api="\${API\_ID}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--api-config="\${CONFIG\_ID}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--location="\${REGION}"

Check that the gateway is active:

gcloud api-gateway gateways describe "\${GATEWAY\_ID}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--location="\${REGION}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--format="yaml(state, defaultHostname, effectiveStreamingMode)"

The output looks like this. New model routing gateways might use this gateway.dev hostname format; older ones keep a run.app hostname.

state: ACTIVE  
defaultHostname: modelrouting-gateway-PROJECT\_NUMBER.us-central1.gateway.dev  
effectiveStreamingMode: EFFECTIVE\_STREAMING\_MODE\_ENABLED

Turn on API key support and create a key that can call only this API:

\# Enable the API's managed service so that API keys work  
export MANAGED\_SERVICE="\$(gcloud api-gateway apis describe "\${API\_ID}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--format='value(managedService)')"  
gcloud services enable "\${MANAGED\_SERVICE}"

\# Create an API key restricted to this API  
gcloud services api-keys create \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--key-id="\${KEY\_ID}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--display-name="Model router client" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--api-target=service="\${MANAGED\_SERVICE}"

API configs are immutable. To change routing later, create a new config and point the gateway at it. To roll back, point the gateway at the previous config.

gcloud api-gateway api-configs create modelrouting-cfg-v2 \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--api="\${API\_ID}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--openapi-spec=apispec.yaml \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--backend-auth-service-account="\${SA\_EMAIL}"

gcloud api-gateway gateways update "\${GATEWAY\_ID}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--api="\${API\_ID}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--api-config=modelrouting-cfg-v2 \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--location="\${REGION}"

## **With Antigravity CLI prompts**

The [Antigravity CLI](https://antigravity.google/docs/getting-started) (agy) is an agent in your terminal. It can write the spec and run the gcloud commands for you. By default, it asks for your approval before it edits files or runs commands. Install it, then start a session in an empty folder. Alternatively you can also use a built in version inside the Google Cloud Shell Editor ([https\://ide.cloud.google.com/](https://ide.cloud.google.com/)).

**Prompt 1: Prepare the project**

Set up my Google Cloud project PROJECT\_ID for API Gateway model routing using gcloud:  
1\. Enable apigateway.googleapis.com, servicemanagement.googleapis.com,  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;servicecontrol.googleapis.com, and aiplatform.googleapis.com.  
2\. Create a service account named model-router-sa and grant it only  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;roles/aiplatform.user on the project.  
3\. Grant my user account roles/iam.serviceAccountUser on that service account.  
Show me each command before you run it, and stop if anything fails.

**Prompt 2: Write the spec**

Read https\://docs.cloud.google.com/api-gateway/docs/model-routing-configure and create  
apispec.yaml, an OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec for API Gateway model routing in project PROJECT\_ID.  
Use the global endpoint https\://aiplatform.googleapis.com for every backend, with  
pathTranslation CONSTANT\_ADDRESS and a 60-second deadline.  
\- POST /v1/chat/gemini-claude uses gemini-claude-router: the default model is  
&nbsp;&nbsp;google/gemini-3.8-flash, with rules for claude-opus-4-7, claude-sonnet-5, and  
&nbsp;&nbsp;claude-haiku-4-5 on their Anthropic :rawPredict endpoints.  
\- POST /v1/chat/maas-models uses maas-models-router: the default model is  
&nbsp;&nbsp;openai/gpt-oss-120b-maas on the /endpoints/openapi/chat/completions endpoint.  
\- Require an API key in the x-api-key header on every operation.  
Check the file against the validation rules on that page before you save it.

**Prompt 3: Deploy**

Deploy apispec.yaml with gcloud. Create the API "modelrouting", an API config  
"modelrouting-cfg-v1" that uses model-router-sa as the backend auth service account,  
and a gateway "modelrouting-gateway" in us-central1. Wait until the gateway is ACTIVE.  
Then enable the API's managed service and print the gateway's defaultHostname and  
effectiveStreamingMode.

**Prompt 4: Create a key and test**

Create an API key with key ID model-router-client, restricted to the modelrouting  
managed service. Then send one request per route through the gateway, always  
including the model field:  
\- claude-opus-4-7 and gemini-3.8-flash on /v1/chat/gemini-claude  
\- openai/gpt-oss-120b-maas on /v1/chat/maas-models  
Show the HTTP status, the response's model field, and the first line of each answer  
in a table. Don't print the API key.

## **Test the model router**

Whichever option you used, set the gateway URL and API key,:

export GATEWAY\_URL="https\://\$(gcloud api-gateway gateways describe "\${GATEWAY\_ID}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--location="\${REGION}" \--format='value(defaultHostname)')"

\# If you created the key in the console, paste it here instead  
export API\_KEY="\$(gcloud services api-keys get-key-string "\${KEY\_ID}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\--format='value(keyString)')"

**Test 1: An explicit rule (Claude Opus 4.7)**

curl \-s \-X POST "\${GATEWAY\_URL}/v1/chat/gemini-claude" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\-H "Content-Type: application/json" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\-H "x-api-key: \${API\_KEY}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\-d '{  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;"model": "claude-opus-4-7",  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;"messages": \[  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;{"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;{"role": "user", "content": "Explain recursion in one sentence."}  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;\]  
&nbsp;&nbsp;}'

**Test 2: Fall back to the default model (Gemini 3.8 Flash)**

curl \-s \-X POST "\${GATEWAY\_URL}/v1/chat/gemini-claude" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\-H "Content-Type: application/json" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\-H "x-api-key: \${API\_KEY}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\-d '{  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;"model": "gemini-3.8-flash",  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;"messages": \[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in five words."}\]  
&nbsp;&nbsp;}'

&nbsp;

**Test 3: The OpenAI-compatible MaaS route (gpt-oss 120B)**

curl \-s \-X POST "\${GATEWAY\_URL}/v1/chat/maas-models" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\-H "Content-Type: application/json" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\-H "x-api-key: \${API\_KEY}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\-d '{  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;"model": "openai/gpt-oss-120b-maas",  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;"messages": \[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in five words."}\]  
&nbsp;&nbsp;}'

&nbsp;

**Test 4: Stream the response**

curl \-N \-s \-X POST "\${GATEWAY\_URL}/v1/chat/gemini-claude" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\-H "Content-Type: application/json" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\-H "x-api-key: \${API\_KEY}" \\  
&nbsp;&nbsp;\-d '{  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;"model": "claude-haiku-4-5",  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;"messages": \[{"role": "user", "content": "Count from 1 to 5."}\],  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;"stream": true  
&nbsp;&nbsp;}'

## **Observe and troubleshoot**

The API's **Overview** tab in the console shows request rates, 95th percentile latency, and 4xx and 5xx error ratios at a glance.

![The API Overview dashboard showing average requests, 95th percentile latency, and 4xx and 5xx error ratios.][image11]

*Fig 10: API Overview monitoring dashboard displaying request traffic and error metrics.*

# **5\. Conclusion**

Model routing turns API Gateway into a managed, OpenAI-compatible front door for Model Garden. Your clients learn one API, your platform team decides in a single OpenAPI spec which model serves each request, and Google runs the infrastructure.

Google Cloud's model lineup makes this especially useful. It's the only hyperscaler that offers all three leading closed-source LLM families, alongside more than 200 other models. You can pick the best model for each task today and change your mind later without touching client code.

The console, gcloud, and the Antigravity CLI all create the same three resources: an API, an API config, and a gateway. Start with one router and a sensible default model, then add rules as you evaluate new models. Keep an eye on the release notes as the Public Preview expands.

* **Read the docs:** [Overview of model routing](https://docs.cloud.google.com/api-gateway/docs/model-routing-overview) and [Configure model routing](https://docs.cloud.google.com/api-gateway/docs/model-routing-configure).  
* **Explore the spec extensions:** [OpenAPI 3.x extensions in API Gateway](https://docs.cloud.google.com/api-gateway/docs/oasv3-extensions).  
* **Secure and tune your gateway:** [Use API keys](https://docs.cloud.google.com/api-gateway/docs/authenticate-api-keys) and [Configure streaming](https://docs.cloud.google.com/api-gateway/docs/streaming-configure).  
* **Browse models:** [Claude on Google Cloud](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/partner-models/claude), [open models on Agent Platform (MaaS)](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/maas/use-open-models), and [OpenAI models on Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/google-cloud-brings-openai-models-to-customers).  
* **Stay current:** [API Gateway release notes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/api-gateway/docs/release-notes).
